definition: Assigning labels to entire time series — arrhythmia types, activity classes — using methods from DTW to transformers.
details: Assigning labels to entire time series — arrhythmia types, activity classes — using methods from DTW to transformers.

explainer.lead: Time series classification assigns a label to an entire time series, such as an arrhythmia type or an activity class. It matters because many real decisions depend on the whole trajectory, not a single point.

tiers.eli5: You look at a whole recording, like a full heart trace, and give it one name, like 'this is the irregular kind', rather than labelling each moment.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose among methods ranging from dynamic time warping to transformers depending on whether shape alignment or learned representations suit the data; a pitfall is that whole-series labels require methods that cope with variable timing.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the task maps a full sequence of observations to a discrete label; supported methods range from DTW-based approaches to transformers. No further formal guarantees are specified here.

explainer.example: Given full recordings of heart activity, the task is to assign each entire recording an arrhythmia type.
